items.title: Ronaldo given 30-day suspension and £215 fine by Portuguese FA
items.summary: Disciplinary council upholds charge against 41-year-old Fifa suspends Egypt’s Hossam Hassan and Mostafa Ziko Cristiano Ronaldo has been suspended for 30 days by the Portuguese ⁠FA after leaving the national team camp following a rift with the coach, ⁠Jorge Jesus, over ⁠his role in the side. The federation’s disciplinary council said it had upheld the charge against ⁠the 41-year-old forward in full and imposed a fine of €255 (£215). Ronaldo left Portugal’s base in ⁠Copenhagen before their Nations League match against Denmark this month, having accused ‌Jesus of twice ‌breaking his word about his role after he was an ‌unused substitute against Norway.

items.title: Palace manager Sage facing fight to keep his job
items.summary: Frenchman under pressure after Brighton thrashing McKenna and Frank among potential replacements Pierre Sage has been granted more time to fix Crystal Palace’s defensive issues but he has been warned that things must improve quickly after the 5-0 defeat at Brighton on Sunday. The Frenchman’s future was in serious doubt after his side conceded three times inside the opening 10 minutes before equalling the 70‑year record for the club’s heaviest defeat against their arch-rivals. The thrashing means Palace have conceded the most goals in the Premier League: 17 from seven games.

items.title: Haaland a doubt, Semenyo out - what are Man City's options?
items.summary: Ghana forward sustained knee injury against Ipswich Maresca to ring changes against AEK Athens on Tuesday Antoine Semenyo has been ruled out for eight weeks with a knee injury, leaving Enzo Maresca short of alternatives to Erling Haaland, who is a doubt for Manchester City’s Champions League game at home against AEK Athens on Tuesday. Semenyo limped off against Ipswich on Saturday and Haaland hobbled off at full time with a foot injury. City are eager to get their European campaign back on track after losing against Paris Saint-Germain last Wednesday.

items.title: England manager Wiegman signs contract extension
items.summary: Wiegman says she ‘cannot think of a better job in football’ She can target three European titles in row with Lionesses Sarina Wiegman has extended her contract to continue as the head coach of England women for Euro 2029. Her deal was due to expire after the World Cup next summer and this extension gives her the chance to lead the Lionesses to three European championship titles in a row. Wiegman, who took on the role in September 2021 , also led her native Netherlands side to European Championship glory in 2017 and has reached the final of the past five major tournaments, twice finishing as a World Cup runner-up.

items.title: Man Utd showed 'unity' in draw with Leeds - Carrick
items.summary: Head coach insists ‘we can still have a really good season’ ‘We were the dominant side,’ says Leeds manager Farke After a week in which Michael Carrick had “the headphones on” to quieten the noise, the Manchester United head coach claimed his side’s 1-1 draw at Leeds on Sunday “felt like a fresh start” and insisted that the season can still be a good one. Carrick’s team have seven points from seven Premier League games and have won only once in the competition, against Ipswich in August. Sunday’s draw followed the previous weekend’s 1-1 draw with Tottenham .

items.title: Hong Kong club hope David Silva can be their hero – but just for one day
items.summary: Former Manchester City player is coming out of retirement at 40 to play one match for ambitious Supreme Sha Tin Hong Kong, China (as is the official football name), has long tried to follow the advice of Han Solo in Return of the Jedi: keeping their distance from China while trying not to look like they are keeping their distance. It is all about maintaining an independent football association and the trappings and privilege that come with it. items.title: UEFA demands answers from FIFA over Infantino dealings in urgent letter
items.summary: European governing body gives two-week deadline Letter addresses other issues including Balogun affair Uefa has given Fifa a two-week deadline to release key documents relating to Gianni Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan and other governance issues in its latest critique of football’s world governing body . A letter sent to Fifa’s general secretary, Mattias Grafström, by his counterpart at Uefa, Theodore Theodoridis, is accompanied by an eight-page document that has more than 50 questions about Fifa’s handling of dozens of issues over the past 12 months. These include the proposed sale of 20% of its commercial rights, the Folarin Balogun affair , the peace prize and relations with Donald Trump and the arrangements for next year’s Fifa presidential election.
